intent: Kept: the ±0.06 m span with 5 sensors and 16 mm footprints, which removed line loss on oval and s-bend. Kept: wheel_track 0.12 and wheel_radius 0.03. Changed: sensor forward offset from y = 0.03 to y = 0.02 (less lag from sensing to wheels, as the Integrator advised for late reactions), body_length from 0.18 to 0.14, and mass from 0.8 to 0.7 kg (about 20 percent less yaw inertia, for faster correction). Expected result: off_track ends reduced, max_error below 0.06 m on more trials, slalom progress above 0.1. Under consideration, not committed: a 7-sensor array at 0.02 m spacing if signal resolution limits the controller, and a shorter wheel_track if the robot is too slow to turn.
learning: Line loss is largely solved by the ±0.06 m span (0 to 0.1 events per run), but max_error still sits at about 0.062 m, so the failure is now tracking lag, not sensing. Test whether shortening sensor lag and yaw inertia reduces max_error. If it does not, the controller's gains are the limit, and I should say so in the next feedback request.
rationale: Race evidence from iteration 1 (entityR2A, 111.8 score, up from 84.6). Widening the array to ±0.06 m with 16 mm footprints did what the previous plan predicted for line loss. Line-loss events fell from 1 per run to 0 on oval and s-bend, and 0.1 on slalom. Every run still ended off_track, and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064 m, just above the 0.06 m limit. rms_error stayed at 0.026 to 0.029 m. So the sensor span was not the only cause: the robot now tracks close to the limit and drifts past it without losing the line. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). Even at body_width 0.18 that is 0.0575, so it stays at 0.06 m. Body width cannot buy margin, and the only geometry levers left are the loop's lag and responsiveness. Integrator feedback (on iteration 0) reported that the robot reacted late on the slalom (progress 0.09 to 0.10). The loop lag is the distance from the sensors to the axle, because the wheels cannot respond until the sensor has read the line, so I am taking that advice: move the sensors from y = 0.03 to y = 0.02 to shorten the lag. I am also reducing yaw inertia, which controls how quickly the body turns in response to a wheel differential. Inertia is m(L²+W²)/12, so cutting body_length from 0.18 to 0.14 and mass from 0.8 to 0.7 kg lowers it by roughly 20 percent. Together these should let the robot correct sooner at the same gains. I am keeping the ±0.06 m span, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track and wheel_radius unchanged, so this race isolates the lag and inertia change. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, max_error below 0.06 m on more trials, and slalom progress rising above 0.1. If max_error still sits at about 0.062 m with lower lag, the cause is the controller's gain balance, not geometry.
